cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Investment in the Next Round
cards.instruction: Describe defeat, penalty, or a bad bargain as a deliberate investment in a larger future win.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Losing the entry fee bought us a complete map of the competition.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. A short-term interpretation of the investment.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then the information has become exclusive. We'll use it selectively.

mechanism: A claims strategic authority over a bad result and directs next action as if the loss deliberately purchased the advantage needed for a larger future win.
confusable: D164 finds immediate benefit; D209 must frame the defeat or cost as intentional investment toward a larger future outcome, not only a lesson.
comparison: Contest entry loss becomes acquired intelligence for a later qualifier; loss-making stall sale becomes paid knowledge applied to a better business choice.
seedUse: Read both cards and four seeds critically. Original larger-win destinations remain vague; preserve the loss and B budget challenge but make the claimed investment and future target concrete.
